summary: Enterprise AI adoption is still very early — earlier than Baker previously thought
summary_extended: Baker argues that enterprise AI adoption is far earlier in its diffusion curve than consensus assumes, citing a striking data point from Anthropic's S-1: despite Anthropic operating at roughly a $67 billion annualized revenue run-rate, only approximately half of the Fortune 500 has adopted it, and AI spending represents just 0.1% of Fortune 500 company expenses. Baker describes this as 'astonishing' and says adoption is 'very early — maybe earlier than I thought we were,' suggesting the market is underestimating the duration and magnitude of the AI spending cycle. The investment implication is a long runway for AI infrastructure and software spend growth, as enterprise penetration has barely begun despite the headline scale of leading AI providers. Baker does not name specific beneficiaries in this thesis segment, but the structural view supports continued growth for AI platform and infrastructure companies broadly.
